strings.name: Ilya Sutskever
strings.summary: Raised in Israel and educated in Canada, Sutskever advanced image recognition, sequence modeling and large language models with collaborators. He co-founded OpenAI and served as chief scientist. He joined the board decision to dismiss Sam Altman in 2023 and left the board after Altman returned. In 2024 he left OpenAI and co-founded SSI, whose goal of safe superintelligence should not be confused with an accomplished result.
strings.coverageNote: Selected milestones verifiable through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: He played a key role in deep learning, sequence modeling and large language model research, and helped establish OpenAI and institutions researching safety.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: University of Toronto: mathematics bachelor’s degree (2005), computer science PhD (2013).
strings.facts.f2.label: Birth information
strings.facts.f2.value: Born in 1986; only the verified year is used.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Collaborative deep learning research
strings.highlights.h1.text: As a co-author of AlexNet and sequence-to-sequence papers, he helped establish influential neural network methods.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Research and safety institutions
strings.highlights.h2.text: He co-founded OpenAI and SSI, putting frontier model research and AI safety on their institutional agendas.
strings.timeline.t1.title: SSI announces compute partnership
strings.timeline.t1.text: SSI and NVIDIA announced a long-term partnership and investment; planned compute expansion did not establish the achievement of superintelligence.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Becomes SSI CEO
strings.timeline.t2.text: SSI confirmed him as CEO and Daniel Levy as president; its technical team continued to report to him.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Co-founds SSI
strings.timeline.t3.text: After leaving OpenAI, he announced Safe Superintelligence with Daniel Gross and Daniel Levy.
strings.timeline.t4.title: OpenAI board crisis
strings.timeline.t4.text: He joined the board decision to dismiss Altman and did not remain on the board after Altman’s return.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Helps found OpenAI
strings.timeline.t5.text: He joined OpenAI’s founding team as a research leader and subsequently served for years as chief scientist.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Sequence-to-sequence learning
strings.timeline.t6.text: With Oriol Vinyals and Quoc Le, he published sequence-to-sequence learning research applied to machine translation.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Co-authors AlexNet paper
strings.timeline.t7.text: With Alex Krizhevsky and Geoffrey Hinton, he advanced ImageNet image classification using a deep convolutional network.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completes mathematics degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: He earned a mathematics bachelor’s degree at Toronto, continued in computer science and received his PhD in 2013.
